transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Gary. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Gary. I received a new Wi-Fi mesh booster pod for our kitchen yesterday, but it won't connect to our Hub 5 router. The little light on the front is just flashing amber constantly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you pair that mesh booster pod to your Hub 5 today, Amara. May I have your account number to begin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is SN 319 8840, under Amara Okafor.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Amara. For security verification, could you please confirm your full installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is 14 Ravensworth Road, London, NW10 5TY. And the security PIN is 9042.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's verified your account, thank you. You have our Fibre 150 package with the Whole Home Mesh Wi-Fi guarantee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly, with the black Hub 5.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to make sure I understand the issue clearly: your main Hub 5 router in the hallway is broadcasting Wi-Fi normally, but the new booster pod in the kitchen is stuck flashing amber and failing to synchronise, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. I work from the kitchen table every day, and my laptop keeps dropping off our team video conferences because the signal from the hallway barely reaches through the walls. It's really frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how annoying that is when you're trying to take video meetings from the kitchen table, Amara. We will get that booster pod paired up and working properly today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Gary, that would be wonderful.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's diagnose where the physical placement is right now. Where in the kitchen is that booster pod currently plugged in?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I plugged it into a socket down behind our large double-door American fridge freezer, right beside the microwave oven so the cables are hidden.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's basic common sense, placing a Wi-Fi unit behind an industrial steel fridge is obviously going to kill the signal. It's not rocket science.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, you don't need to be condescending about it. Your instruction leaflet didn't say anything about staying away from kitchen appliances.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Metal appliances and microwave shielding reflect 5 gigahertz radio waves completely. The pod cannot receive the pairing beacon through two hundred kilograms of steel.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, fine. Where should I put it then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It needs to be plugged into an open wall socket, roughly halfway between the main Hub in the hallway and your kitchen table, on a clear surface.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is a double power socket right above the wooden breakfast bar on the kitchen counter, with clear line of sight to the hallway door.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That breakfast bar socket is in a much better location. Please unplug the pod from behind the fridge and move it over there now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, unplugged from behind the fridge... plugging into the breakfast bar socket now. Power switch on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What is the front light doing as it powers on? It should cycle through white and then begin flashing slowly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was solid white for ten seconds, and now it is pulsing a slow amber light.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Pulsing amber means it is ready to pair via Wi-Fi Protected Setup. Walk over to your Hub 5 in the hallway, please.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Standing in front of the Hub 5 in the hallway now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On the side of the Hub 5, you will find a small circular button marked with two curved arrows forming a circle. That is the WPS pairing button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I see the WPS button with the two arrows.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Press and hold that WPS button for three seconds until the front light bar on the Hub 5 starts pulsing blue, then let go.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Holding down... one, two, three... and released. The light bar on the Hub 5 is pulsing blue now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now walk straight back to the kitchen booster pod and press the small sync button on the back of the pod for two seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Walking back into the kitchen... pressing the sync button on the pod for two seconds... released. The pod light is pulsing blue as well now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Both units are now exchanging encrypted cryptographic keys over the 5 gigahertz backhaul. This handshake takes about forty-five seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Still pulsing blue on both devices...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once paired, the pod's front LED will turn solid green, which signifies an optimal connection speed to the primary Hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait... it just turned solid green! And the Hub 5 in the hallway has returned to its normal solid white light!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to verify now that the handshake has finalized, is the booster pod maintaining a steady solid green light without dipping back to amber?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, rock solid green. It hasn't flickered once.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can see the pod registered on our cloud network management system now. It is linked with a minus 52 dBm signal strength, which provides full bandwidth throughput.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's great. Let me test my work laptop here at the kitchen table.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, please connect your laptop and check your Wi-Fi signal icon. It should seamlessly roam to the booster pod's stronger BSSID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening my laptop... Wi-Fi has connected instantly with all four bars full! Let me run an online speed test.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please run a speed test and read back the download speed, upload speed, and ping latency measurements.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's hitting 154 megabits per second download and 28 megabits upload, with a 9 millisecond ping! Before this, I was barely getting 8 megabits at this table!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is delivering the full capacity of your Fibre 150 connection directly to your workspace. The breakfast bar placement provides a completely clear radio path.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And my Microsoft Teams call status has switched from 'Poor network' to 'Excellent connection'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So to confirm, Amara: the mesh booster pod is successfully paired, the LED is steady solid green, and your kitchen laptop is receiving full 154 Mbps speeds?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 100 percent resolved. The technical solution worked like a charm, even if your earlier comment was a bit sharp.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am pleased the technical issue is fully resolved for your work. I have logged the optimal placement details on your account records for future reference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We will leave it plugged in right there on the counter. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can also use our S-Net Home app to monitor all connected devices and check their individual signal strengths whenever you like.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. I will download the app this evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your broadband, router settings, or landline that I can assist you with today, Amara?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was the only problem and it's working now. Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome. I hope your video conferences run smoothly for the rest of your working day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Gary, have a good day.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Amara. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Take care.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have a great day ahead, Amara.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.
